plan.title: Simple Pine Bookcase
plan.summary: A freestanding 800 × 300 × 1800 mm bookcase with three adjustable-in-position (fixed during assembly) shelves, butt joints, screws, and a thin plywood back to resist racking. Anchor it to a wall stud to reduce tip-over risk.
assumptions: Dimensions are the finished outside dimensions; the 6 mm back is applied to the rear, giving 300 mm total depth.
Use 18 mm pine plywood or pine-faced project panels for the sides, top, bottom, and shelves. Cut the panel depth to 294 mm so the back brings the total depth to 300 mm.
The bookcase has three fixed shelves, positioned 450, 900, and 1350 mm above the bottom. Shelf positions can be changed before assembly if different book heights are needed.
The plan is for ordinary household books distributed across the shelves, not concentrated heavy loads. Secure the finished bookcase to a wall stud.
The back is 6 mm plywood. Its edges meet the rear edges of the carcass; screws through it into the shelf and carcass edges act as real fastening joinery.
Pine plywood and cut-to-size availability vary. Confirm actual sheet thickness before cutting; keep all carcass panels the same actual thickness.

parts.name: Side panels
parts.notes: Full-height sides. The right side starts at x=782, leaving 764 mm between the sides.

parts.name: Top and bottom panels
parts.notes: Fit between the side panels. Bottom occupies y=0–18; top occupies y=1782–1800.

parts.name: Fixed shelves
parts.notes: Fixed shelves with their bottom faces at the listed y positions. Each fits between the side panels.

parts.name: Back panel
parts.notes: Covers the rear and brings overall depth to 300 mm.

hardware.name: Coarse-thread wood screws for carcass
hardware.notes: Four per top, bottom, and shelf panel: two through each side into each panel end. Predrill to reduce splitting.

hardware.name: Screws for back panel
hardware.notes: Fasten through the 6 mm back into the rear edges of the sides, top, bottom, and shelves; predrill the back only.

hardware.name: Anti-tip brackets
hardware.notes: Use both brackets at the top of the bookcase. Fasten the wall side into a stud with suitable screws; do not rely on drywall alone.

hardware.name: Screws for anti-tip brackets
hardware.size: 5 × 60 mm stud screws; bracket-side screws as supplied
hardware.notes: Two 5 × 60 mm screws to secure the brackets to a wall stud. Use the bracket manufacturer's supplied screws to attach brackets to the bookcase.

finishes.name: Water-based clear polyurethane
finishes.notes: Apply two thin coats, following the product label for sanding and recoat time. Allow the final coat to cure fully before loading books.

tools.name: Tape measure and pencil
tools.alternative: A ruler and a fine-point marker can substitute for small measurements.

tools.name: Combination square or carpenter's square
tools.alternative: Use a straight, verified 90-degree corner and carefully compare diagonals.

tools.name: Circular saw with straightedge guide
tools.alternative: Have the home center make the straight panel cuts, or use a hand saw with a clamped guide.

tools.name: Drill/driver with bits and countersink bit
tools.alternative: A hand drill and screwdriver work, but take extra care to keep pilot holes straight.

tools.name: Clamps
tools.alternative: Ask a helper to hold aligned pieces while you start screws; do not put hands near a drill bit.

tools.name: Sandpaper or random-orbit sander
tools.alternative: Sand by hand with a sanding block.

tools.name: Paintbrush or finish applicator
tools.alternative: Use a clean lint-free cloth only if the finish label allows wiping application.

tools.name: Safety glasses, hearing protection, and dust mask
tools.alternative: Do not substitute for eye protection; use suitable protection whenever cutting, drilling, or sanding.

tools.name: Stud finder
tools.alternative: Locate a stud using a reliable wall-stud method and confirm its position before drilling.

steps.title: Check materials and cut panels
steps.text: Confirm the actual panel thickness, then cut P1 (side panels), P2 (top and bottom panels), P3 (fixed shelves), and P4 (back panel) to the listed dimensions. Have sheet goods cut at the store if you do not have a suitable saw and guide. Label each piece and check that matching panels are the same size.
tools_used: Safety glasses, hearing protection, and dust mask
steps.safety: Wear eye, hearing, and dust protection. Support sheet goods fully and keep hands clear of the blade; unplug or remove the battery before adjustments.
steps.tip: Measure each cut from the same reference edge, and verify the 764 mm pieces fit between the 18 mm sides.

steps.title: Sand and mark the panels
steps.text: Lightly sand the cut edges and faces of P1, P2, P3, and P4. On the inside face of each P1 side, mark the bottom panel, three shelf positions, and top panel; use the same measurements on both sides. Mark shelf panel bottom edges at 450, 900, and 1350 mm from the bottom.
tools_used: Safety glasses, hearing protection, and dust mask
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection while sanding, and secure the panels so they cannot slide.
steps.tip: Use a square to carry each shelf line across the side panel; mismatched marks make shelves crooked.

steps.title: Drill carcass pilot holes
steps.text: Lay each P1 side flat with its inside face up. At every marked panel position, drill two evenly spaced pilot holes through the side panel, positioned to enter the center of the 18 mm panel edge; countersink the outside face just enough for screw heads to sit flush. Do not drill oversized holes in the shelf or top/bottom ends.
tools_used: Drill/driver with bits and countersink bit
steps.safety: Clamp the panel securely and wear eye protection. Keep the drill perpendicular to the panel and fingers away from the bit.
steps.tip: Practice the pilot-hole size on an offcut; the screw should bite firmly without splitting the panel edge.

steps.title: Dry-fit the carcass
steps.text: Place one P1 side inside-face up on a flat surface. Fit P2 (bottom panel), all three P3 shelves, and the other P2 (top panel) between the sides at their marked locations. Check that the front edges align and the assembly measures 800 mm wide before fastening.
steps.safety: Use a helper for positioning the large side panels, and keep the assembly supported so it cannot tip or slide.
steps.tip: The panel ends must meet the inside faces of the sides; do not force a tight fit by bowing a side panel.

steps.title: Screw together the carcass
steps.text: Apply a thin bead of wood glue to each end joint if desired, then assemble P2 (top and bottom panels) and P3 (shelves) between the P1 sides. Drive two 4 × 50 mm screws through each side into each panel end, using the pilot holes; use 20 screws total. Check square as you tighten and wipe away squeezed-out glue.
tools_used: Drill/driver with bits and countersink bit
steps.safety: Keep the bookcase supported while driving screws, wear eye protection, and use a low driver setting to avoid stripping or overdriving screws.
steps.tip: Tighten gradually, alternating sides, and recheck that the front edges are flush and the carcass is square.

steps.title: Attach the back panel
steps.text: Lay the carcass face down on a clean, flat surface. Set P4 (back panel) flush with all outside edges, then measure both diagonals and adjust the carcass until they match. Predrill the 6 mm back and fasten it with 3 × 20 mm screws around the perimeter and into each shelf line, using 42 screws total.
tools_used: Drill/driver with bits and countersink bit
steps.safety: Get help to turn the carcass face down; keep hands clear of pinch points and support the piece on a stable surface.
steps.tip: The back helps keep the bookcase square, so do not fasten it until the diagonal measurements match.

steps.title: Sand the assembled bookcase
steps.text: Fill visible screw recesses if desired, then lightly sand exposed edges and faces, working with the grain. Remove all sanding dust with a vacuum or clean cloth before applying finish. Check that no screw points protrude.
tools_used: Safety glasses, hearing protection, and dust mask
steps.safety: Wear eye and dust protection, and keep the bookcase stable while sanding. Avoid inhaling fine dust.
steps.tip: Ease sharp corners with a few light sanding strokes rather than rounding them noticeably.

steps.title: Apply finish
steps.text: Apply two thin coats of water-based clear polyurethane to exposed surfaces, following the label's application and recoat directions. Let each coat dry for the label's stated time and lightly sand between coats only if the product instructions call for it. Keep the bookcase unloaded until the finish has cured.
steps.safety: Work with good ventilation, keep finish away from flames, and follow the product label for skin, eye, and vapor protection.
steps.tip: Thin coats are less likely to sag on the tall sides; check for drips along shelf edges before they dry.

steps.title: Stand and anchor the bookcase
steps.text: With a helper, stand the bookcase in its intended location and check that it sits level. Locate a wall stud behind the top of the unit and attach both anti-tip brackets using the bracket maker's instructions and the 5 × 60 mm stud screws. Attach the brackets to the bookcase with the supplied fasteners; do not anchor only into drywall.
tools_used: Drill/driver with bits and countersink bit
steps.safety: Use a helper when lifting and standing the tall bookcase. Keep the unit secured from tipping while locating and fastening the brackets.
steps.tip: If the wall is masonry or the stud location is unsuitable, use a fixing system rated for that wall and load rather than a basic drywall anchor.

steps.title: Load the shelves
steps.text: After the finish has fully cured, place books evenly across the three P3 shelves, starting at the bottom and distributing weight rather than stacking it in one spot. Recheck that the unit remains level and that both anti-tip brackets are secure. Do not climb on the shelves or use the bookcase as a ladder.
steps.safety: Keep children from climbing or hanging on the bookcase, and maintain the anti-tip connection to the wall.
steps.tip: If a shelf visibly bends under its intended books, unload it and add a properly supported shelf rather than continuing to use it.

safety_overview: Wear safety glasses during cutting and drilling, hearing protection around power saws, and a dust mask when cutting or sanding sheet goods.
Clamp panels securely before cutting, drilling, or sanding; keep hands away from blades and drill bits.
Get help lifting and standing the tall carcass, and keep it supported until it is anchored.
Anchor the finished bookcase to a wall stud with anti-tip brackets. Drywall alone is not a suitable fixing for this tall unit.
Use the finish only with good ventilation and follow its label for handling, drying, and curing.
